question:
[MCQ] Based on the clip, what visual check is used to decide which of the two side-by-side tubes is the artery?
A. Look for spontaneous pulsation of one structure
B. Apply gentle probe pressure and identify the vessel that remains relatively noncompressible as the artery
C. Use color Doppler and select the channel with predominantly pulsatile flow as the artery
D. Identify the tube with a thicker, more echogenic wall and a smaller, rounder lumen as the artery
groundtruth: The operator differentiates the paired vessels by observing their behavior, identifying the pulsatile structure as the carotid artery.

question:
[MCQ] The clip shows an additional maneuver applied to the two vessels to confirm which is which. What is done, and why?
A. Activate color Doppler to identify the vein by continuous low-velocity flow versus the artery by pulsatile flow.
B. Ask the patient to perform a Valsalva maneuver to transiently dilate the vein and help differentiate it from the artery.
C. Apply probe compression, to confirm vessel identity by compressibility
D. Use spectral Doppler waveform analysis to distinguish the artery by high-resistance pulsatility from the vein by phasic respiratory variation.
groundtruth: The operator applies probe pressure over the vessels and observes compression behavior to confirm the anatomic identification.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the clip, what probe movement is used to change imaging planes, and what is the goal?
A. Rotate the probe ~90°, to obtain a long-axis view of the vessel
B. Fan/tilt the probe through the vessel, to sweep adjacent anatomy and ensure you have not mistaken a vein for an artery.
C. Slide the probe along the vessel’s course, to keep the vessel centered in the same transverse plane for tracking and confirmation.
D. Rock (heel-toe) the probe to optimize insonation angle, to improve vessel wall definition without changing from short-axis.
groundtruth: The operator rotates the probe 90 degrees to transition from transverse to a longitudinal (sagittal) view of the carotid.

question:
[MCQ] The clip shows a control change made to clean up the grayscale image. What is adjusted, and what is the reason?
A. Reduce TGC, to suppress noise/clutter
B. Reduce overall 2D gain, to decrease background speckle without altering depth-dependent amplification.
C. Move the focal zone deeper, to sharpen the region of interest and reduce apparent blur in the far field.
D. Lower the dynamic range (increase compression), to improve contrast and make tissue interfaces stand out.
groundtruth: The operator reduces TGC to clear noise/artifacts and improve grayscale image clarity.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the clip, which imaging mode is enabled next, and what is the purpose?
A. Power Doppler, to increase sensitivity for low‑velocity flow when color signal is weak
B. Color Doppler, to map flow within the target vessel
C. M‑mode, to document cyclic wall motion and measure vessel diameter changes over time
D. Spectral (pulsed‑wave) Doppler, to quantify peak systolic velocity and waveform morphology in the vessel
groundtruth: Color Doppler is activated and a color box is positioned over the artery to visualize flow.

question:
[MCQ] The clip shows a refinement of the color overlay to improve interpretability. What is changed, and why?
A. Reduce color gain, to prevent color “bleeding” beyond the vessel
B. Narrow the color box, to improve frame rate and spatial resolution of the flow overlay
C. Increase color scale (PRF), to reduce aliasing and better display higher-velocity flow
D. Raise the wall filter, to suppress low-frequency tissue motion (clutter) and clarify true vascular flow
groundtruth: The operator reduces color gain to achieve proper intraluminal color filling without bleed artifacts while visualizing the common carotid artery.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the sequence in the clip, what workflow phase is the operator in?
A. Optimizing color Doppler to localize flow and confirm direction before placing a spectral Doppler gate
B. Reviewing a previously saved Doppler tracing and measuring velocities during post-processing rather than acquiring a new sample
C. Acquiring and evaluating a spectral Doppler velocity sample
D. Optimizing B-mode image quality (depth, gain, focal zone) to better visualize the target vessel prior to Doppler
groundtruth: The operator activates PW Doppler, centers the sample gate, freezes, and inspects the spectral trace to document a quality waveform from the common carotid artery.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the clip, what probe motion is used to progress to the next key landmark along the vessel, and what is the intent?
A. Slide the probe superiorly along the vessel, to reach the next characteristic segment before branching
B. Rock the probe to optimize the Doppler insonation angle and confirm flow within the current segment rather than advancing along the vessel.
C. Rotate the probe 90° to obtain a transverse short-axis view to assess patency and surrounding structures at the same level.
D. Fan/sweep the probe side-to-side to relocate the vessel after it drifts out of plane, without intentionally moving to the next landmark.
groundtruth: The operator returns to transverse view and slides the probe cephalad, following the common carotid artery until the morphology changes approaching the bulb region.

question:
[MCQ] The clip shows that the initial spectral Doppler tracing at this new location is suboptimal, followed by a corrective adjustment. What is the adjustment, and why?
A. Increase the Doppler scale/PRF to reduce aliasing and better display higher peak velocities.
B. Optimize Doppler gain and wall filter settings to improve signal-to-noise while minimizing low-frequency motion artifact.
C. Reposition and narrow the sample volume to the center of the lumen to avoid wall contamination and spectral broadening.
D. Steer/angle the Doppler beam, to improve insonation angle and flow signal
groundtruth: At the bulb, PW Doppler initially shows a poor waveform; the operator steers the Doppler beam to correct the angle and improve the flow signal before documenting velocity.

question:
[MCQ] Based on the later clip sequence, what broader objective is being pursued, and what method is used to confirm it?
A. Differentiating an artery from a vein in the region and confirming with pulsed Doppler waveform analysis
B. Identifying where one vessel splits into two branches and confirming with color flow
C. Localizing a focal stenosis in the vessel and confirming hemodynamic significance with spectral Doppler velocities
D. Assessing for vascular patency or thrombosis in a single vessel and confirming with color Doppler flow filling
groundtruth: The operator scans superior to the bulb to locate the bifurcation, uses color Doppler to confirm two distinct vessels, and sweeps through the region to verify the transition from one vessel to two (ICA/ECA).
